stem: Which statement shows how this excerpt is an example of transcendentalism in the early-to-mid 1800s?

options.label: F
options.text: Thoreau uses reason to explain natural events that happen in the world.

options.label: G
options.text: Thoreau focuses on the role of science in changing the natural world.

options.label: H
options.text: Thoreau studies the relationship between nature and historical events.

options.label: J
options.text: Thoreau focuses on the relationship between humans and the natural world.

visual_elements: The most sweet and tender, the most innocent and encouraging society may be found in any natural object, even for the . . . most melancholy man. There can be no very black melancholy to him who lives in the midst of Nature and has his senses still. . . . While I enjoy the friendship of the seasons I trust that nothing can make life a burden to me. —Henry David Thoreau, Walden, 1854
